functions.description: Compute the one-sample t statistic, degrees of freedom and standard error of the mean from the sample size, sample mean, sample standard deviation and hypothesized mean.
inputs: the sample size n, the number of observations in the sample
the sample mean of the measured quantity with its unit
the sample standard deviation of the measured quantity with its unit
the hypothesized population mean under the null hypothesis, with its unit
outputs: the standard error of the mean

functions.description: Look up the two-tailed critical t value for a significance level and degrees of freedom.
inputs: the significance level alpha for the two-tailed test
the degrees of freedom n-1

functions.description: Compute the two-sided p-value of a t statistic with given degrees of freedom.
inputs: the test statistic t
the degrees of freedom n-1

functions.description: Decide whether to reject the null hypothesis by comparing the absolute test statistic with the two-tailed critical value.
inputs: the test statistic t
the two-tailed critical t value
outputs: the reject or fail to reject decision

functions.description: Construct a confidence interval for the population mean from the sample statistics and the two-tailed critical t value, and check whether the hypothesized mean lies inside it.
inputs: the sample size n, the number of observations in the sample
the sample mean of the measured quantity with its unit
the sample standard deviation of the measured quantity with its unit
the hypothesized population mean under the null hypothesis, with its unit
the two-tailed critical t value
outputs: the confidence interval lower and upper bounds
the agreement between the interval and the test decision

functions.description: Test whether a population mean differs from a hypothesized value at a given significance level and report the test statistic and conclusion.
inputs: the sample size n, the number of observations in the sample
the sample mean of the measured quantity with its unit
the sample standard deviation of the measured quantity with its unit
the hypothesized population mean under the null hypothesis, with its unit
the significance level alpha for the two-tailed test
outputs: the test statistic t with degrees of freedom
the reject or fail to reject decision
the final reported conclusion about the mean

entry_points.text: A sample of ●1 bolts has a mean length of ●2 and a sample standard deviation of ●3. At ●5, test whether the true mean length differs from ●4. Give the test statistic and your conclusion.

params.description: the sample size n, the number of observations in the sample
params.validity_range: Must be an integer of at least 2, so that degrees of freedom n-1 is at least 1; larger n gives a more precise standard error, and very small n makes the t critical values large.

params.description: the sample mean of the measured quantity with its unit
params.validity_range: Any real number in the same unit as the hypothesized mean and the standard deviation; no sign restriction for a general measured quantity, but the unit must match the hypothesized mean.

params.description: the sample standard deviation of the measured quantity with its unit
params.validity_range: Must be strictly positive (greater than 0); a zero standard deviation would make the t statistic undefined, and it must be expressed in the same unit as the sample mean.

params.description: the hypothesized population mean under the null hypothesis, with its unit
params.validity_range: Any real number in the same unit as the sample mean; it is the value tested in the null hypothesis H0 that the true mean equals it.

params.description: the significance level alpha for the two-tailed test
params.validity_range: Must lie strictly between 0 and 1; conventional values are 0.01, 0.05 and 0.10, and smaller alpha gives larger critical values and a stricter rejection rule.

entry_points.text: A sample of 36 bolts has a mean length of 50.4 mm and a sample standard deviation of 1.2 mm. At α = 0.05, test whether the true mean length differs from 50 mm. Give the test statistic and your conclusion.
